title: Basket weave brick and concrete pavers
purpose: Generate tileable PBR maps of pavers laid in basket weave: two, three or four pavers per square turning in a checkerboard, with sand joints, worn rounded edges, fired flashing, settling and optional moss. Use for patios, garden paths, courtyards and sidewalks.

contract.signature: generate(width=256, height=256, seed=0, preset="default", directx_normal=False, **parameters) -> {map name: {"channels", "colour_space", "pixels"}}
contract.command_line: python basketweave_pavers.py --size 1024 --seed 7 --preset NAME --out DIR [--width W --height H] [--set NAME=VALUE] [--directx-normal] [--orm]

parameters.name: bricks_per_square
parameters.meaning: Pavers side by side in each square; the paver length is this many paver widths.

parameters.name: repeats
parameters.meaning: Pairs of checkerboard squares across the tile.

parameters.name: joint_fill
parameters.meaning: Height of the sand in the joints relative to the paver tops.

parameters.name: edge_wear
parameters.meaning: Rounding and chipping of the paver edges from traffic.

parameters.name: flashing
parameters.meaning: Darker fired ends and blotches on clay pavers.

parameters.name: settling
parameters.meaning: Uneven paver heights and tilts from a settled bed.

parameters.name: moss
parameters.meaning: Moss and dark dirt growing in the joints.

parameters.name: hue_shift
parameters.meaning: Hue rotation of the albedo in turns.

presets.name: default
presets.description: Red clay pavers in two-paver basket weave with light sand joints.

presets.name: charcoal_concrete
presets.description: Charcoal concrete pavers in three-paver basket weave, crisp chamfers.

presets.name: weathered_moss
presets.description: Old brown brick pavers, worn round, settled, with moss in the joints.

presets.name: buff_patio
presets.description: Buff and tan clay pavers with grey sand and light flashing.

limits: Pavers are rectangles whose length equals the square side, so the layout is the plain basket weave only; half basket and diagonal variants, borders and cut pavers are out of scope. Flashing, chips, settling and moss are noise-driven approximations. Colours are artistic, not measured. Occlusion is a blurred-height estimate, not ray traced.
technique_references: Checkerboard of squares with alternating paver orientation
Rectangle side distances for joints and rounded edges
Per-paver hashing for colour, flashing, tilt and roughness
Fractional Brownian motion of tileable gradient noise
Height to tangent-space normal by central differences
